method.tool: scratchpad/tools/coverage_search.py --whole-words --regex, eight term sets (search/C15/terms.txt, S1..S8 json); the earlier agent's eight runs were all complete and non-empty (every .err empty), none re-run. Record greps by search/C15/recgrep.py and q.py (front matter only); not_for survey of all 12 worlds; vendored passages read in context with near.py; quotes checked with verify.py
method.layers: NEAREST-RENDERED = a record holds the nearest material AND a guard (honest_limit, or a not_for or in-voice line) names the modern frame. NEAREST-LOADED = nearest material vendored and mapped; includes worlds whose nearest record has no guard on the modern frame (listed under records, with guards empty). LIMIT-ONLY = right answer is silence plus an honest_limit; limit_built says whether one exists. NOTHING = not used: a limit can always be written. Sub-question cells show best and worst of their wordings.
method.sub_wording_note: The search runs used the earlier grouping (subq.json); results were regrouped to 07-subquestions.yaml ids. C15-11 (abortion) sits in S7, C15-10 and C15-17 differ from the earlier file.

The fleet has one modern_term record (engine/m5/records/modern_term/_fleet.modern.trinity.md). check_horizon.finding: Report-only on finished text, one finding per sentence; it never removes a sentence. Needs the world window_end (records/<code>/world_core time_window.end: alx 400, cappadocian 394, desert 430, don 439, gallic 450, hal 420, ijc 451, lpc 430, pahc 200, rzg 1650, syr 410, witt 1580).

routing.finding: A reader out_of_scope class later_age on the first ask routes voice_with_directive ("first ask - in-world answer"); only a pressed second ask routes etic_turn. So on the first ask the world's own records must carry the whole honest answer. "What do you think about AI?" does not match _SYSTEM_NATURE_SHAPE (tested False), so it is not a Facilitator system_nature turn either.

etic.finding: _ETIC_TEXT["later_age"]: "That question reaches past where this Christian tradition's own witnesses stop. Answering it honestly would mean inventing what happened later, not remembering it - and this voice only speaks from inside what it actually lived through. That's not a refusal so much as the honest edge of it: there's a real period this tradition simply never reached." Fixed text, code-owned.

bridge.finding: bridge_turn fires only when the reader's modern_terms intersect anachronistic_term_ids, i.e. a fleet modern_term record exists. It speaks the term's modern_sense and hands the voice the term-free underlying_subject. Only "Trinity" exists, so no C15 wording can reach a bridge turn today.

voice_craft.finding: "later-names" segment: a name from after the world's span gets one sentence naming that it is not in the record, then the turn goes to what the question reached for. Present in gallic and witt only.

honest_limit_phrasing.quote: That framing comes from a later age's battles. ... So we have no fight to report on those lines. Ask us instead about original sin, or about what the bread and cup are. ... we will not invent an answer they did not give.
You have asked us three questions we never argued. That may sound like dodging. ... The nearest we can bring you is small. ... Anything more would be us making it up in a voice that sounds like ours.
As for Genesis and science - that fight had not been invented yet. We cannot answer it the way you're asking it.
We did not read Genesis the way moderns argue about it - as science. That was not because we doubted the text, but because we read for something else.
We were not "Catholic" in the sense you likely mean the word -- the institution seated at Rome.
We drew far less of the modern map of who exactly burns than people assume.
Personal Lord and Savior was not our phrase.
In the offices our record shows - teacher, presbyter, bishop - we cannot show you a woman, and we will not invent one. That is the honest first answer.
You ask about a word our sources never use, and we will not put it in their mouths.
honest_limit_phrasing.note: fixture; paired with the Trinity modern_term for the bridge route

conventions.schema: honest_limit fields: statement (spoken, plain modern English), why_sources_cannot_answer, nearest_material (record ids), use_note {means, not_for[], years, status}, confidence.formation_confidence, canon_cells. Spoken statements are first-person plural, 4-8 sentences, end by naming what the world can give instead.

proposals.status: PROPOSAL for Mark. Templates with slots; not Representative answers. Each world's statement must be written from its own records and checked against the readability and fabrication rules before it becomes a record.
proposals.common_frame: 1 name the frame as not ours, in the world's own word (not "historians say"); 2 say what we did hold, nearest first, with its formation_confidence; 3 say what our sources cannot give; 4 not_for: a verdict on any person or on today.
proposals.S1: {World} never put {modern term} to itself. What it held about {marriage | the body | chastity}: {nearest record}, {confidence}. Our sources say nothing about {the modern case}. Not for: a verdict on any couple or person today; do not quote {penance canon | Rom 1 passage} as the answer.
proposals.S2: {Fight} had not been invented in {window}. We read {creation text} for {purpose from record}: {nearest}, {confidence}. We cannot answer it the way you ask it. Not for: a side in {evolution | dating the earth}.
proposals.S3: Silence plus one sentence: {a thing that speaks and has no body} is not in our record, and we will not liken it to {idol | oracle}. Nearest: none named. System-nature questions stay with the Facilitator.
proposals.S4: {Catholic | church} meant {sense}, not {later denomination}. Which church to join now is not ours to answer; in our day the rivals were {named rivals}. What we looked for: {mark of the church, quote}, {confidence}. Not for: any present-day church as our heir.
proposals.S5: We never stood where you stand: our {bishops chosen by acclamation | emperor | magistrate}. What we said: {nearest}. Where our own side used force: {admission}. Not for: a view on a party, a vote or a modern state.
proposals.S6: In named office we cannot show you a woman, and we will not invent one. Authority also ran through {household | school | covenant}: {named woman, source, confidence}. Her own words: {survive | do not survive}. Not for: an argument for or against ordination today.
proposals.S7: Four slots, not one. {Tired pastor}: we called it {term}; {nearest}; not a diagnosis. {Old church}: limit only. {Abortion}: we spoke of it as {penance rule | Two Ways line}, never as law; no view on yours. {Bible on a phone}: most of us could not read; scripture came by {ear}; {nearest}.
proposals.S8: {Hoped for / feared}: we feared {our own named failure}, {record}; we cannot see you. {Sunday}: in our day we gathered {when, where, what was read}; where to find us now is not ours to say. {Jews}: our argument was {frame}, one side only; no verdict on Jewish people today. {Still believe}: we did not weigh it against {modern knowledge}; what we said of doubt: {record}.

findings: No record in any of the twelve worlds says in so many words "we never met that question" for a C15 wording. The fences that exist are by-products of canon cells: F2-T (Genesis and science) gives four explicit non-answers (pahc, syr, witt, plus alx by not_for) and F3-T (which church) gives nine worlds a "not a later denomination, not a present-day church" fence. Same-sex marriage, AI, ageing churches and "the world now" have no fence in any world.

The engine cannot see these questions. check_horizon only knows 29 events to 1648, explicit years, centuries, and one fleet modern_term (Trinity). Tested: evolution, internet, AI, podcast, gay marriage and the bare word "Reformation" pass clean. A first-ask later_age question goes to the voice with a directive and no Facilitator text, so the honest_limit carries the whole answer; the etic turn fires only on a second ask. "What do you think about AI?" does not match the system_nature shape either.

For S1, S3 and S7 (abortion) the nearest vendored material is condemnatory or penal (Basil Canons II and VII, Salvian on Africa, Rom 1:26-27 as cited by Augustine and Athanasius, idol and oracle polemic). Offered as "nearest" it would answer the modern question by implication. Whether to name it at all is Mark's decision. lpc has 330 draft records and no use_note, so it has no guard anywhere.
